newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says mark correction exaggerated.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says mark correction exaggerated.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Wednesday after a cabinet meeting that the current weakness of the mark against major currencies reflected a normal correction.
But he added that the movements in exchange rates were now somewhat overdone, saying: "What is happening now is partly a normalisation. The swings are exaggerated."
Rexrodt was speaking before a news conference unrelated to foreign exchange matters.

When asked whether the cabinet planned to issue a statement on foreign exchange market developments, he replied: "Perhaps the economic fundamentals in the Anglo-Saxon countries are better ...," but then stopped short and added: "Cabinet discussed this."
The government is expected to comment on forex developments at a regular news conference at 1230 GMT, government sources said earlier on Wednesday.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday that Germany was interested in a strong mark and a strong European monetary union and that the cabinet would issue a statement on forex developments after its meeting on Wednesday.
